VISIT NOTE (draft)

**Patient:** Ms. Hill
**Age/Sex:** 41-year-old female

**Chief complaint:** Right middle finger pain.

**History of present illness:** Patient reports pain at the end of the right middle finger for four to five days, since a motor vehicle accident on Saturday. She was stopped at a four-way stop when she was rear-ended by a vehicle whose driver she believes was texting. She was angry at the other driver, made an obscene gesture, and struck the ceiling of her car with the finger. Car damage was minor (trunk crumpled). She reports no other injuries.

**Past history noted in visit:** Atrial fibrillation. Currently takes digoxin.

**Examination:** Tenderness over the distal phalanx of the right middle finger, with pain on pressure at that site. Pressure at the other site tested was not painful. Clinician notes the remainder of the exam is normal.

**Imaging:** Right middle finger x-ray reviewed with patient. Fracture at the tip of the middle finger involving the distal phalanx.

**Assessment:** Fracture of the distal phalanx of the right middle finger (third finger), following motor vehicle accident.

**Plan:**
- Tramadol 50 mg PO every 6 hours as needed for pain; dispense 8 tablets (about two days' supply).
- Finger splint applied.
- Follow-up in 2 weeks with repeat x-ray.
- Patient asked about tramadol with digoxin; clinician stated it will be okay.

**Assessment and Plan:**
1. **Back pain:** Likely recurrence of kidney stones.

Patient: George (last name not stated in transcript)
Visit type: Office visit
Clinician: Not named in transcript

**Chief complaint:** Numbness and tingling in the fingers and pain in the wrist/hand.

**History of present illness:**

- Onset was gradual and spontaneous. Patient does not recall a specific cause.
- Symptoms occur mainly at night. Patient wakes with the hand asleep and has to shake it out.
- Numbness involves all fingers, more prominent in the thumb and index finger. Patient also reports occasional numbness in the little finger.

- Patient reports no problems with the right hand. Patient's statements about laterality (right vs. left) are inconsistent in the transcript and should be verified.

**Occupational history:** Landscaping. Heavy labor with repetitive raking and digging, performed daily.

**Social history:** Alcohol use of one to two beers on Fridays and Saturdays.

- Respiratory: A little bit of stridor noted. No wheezes or rales.
- Abdomen: No rebound or guarding.
- HEENT/Skin: Head symmetrical. Mucous membranes normal. Not hot to touch.
- Right foot:
